---
title: "Quiz: the 2D wavelet transform"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. Subbands: **LL** (approximation), **V** (high-pass along $x$: vertical edges), **H** (high-pass along $y$: horizontal edges), **D** (diagonal).

---

**Q1.** How is the 2D wavelet transform computed from the 1D one?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
As for the 2D DFT.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Separably: one level of the 1D filter bank on every row (low-pass half left, high-pass half right), then on every column of the result (low top, high bottom). This gives the four subbands; further levels repeat this on LL only.
:::

---

**Q2.** An image shows a single vertical line. Which detail band at level 1 lights up?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Along which axis does the image change?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**V**: the image changes along $x$ (across the line), so the band that is high-pass along $x$ responds. Along $y$ the line is constant, so H and D stay near 0 (except at the line's ends).
:::

---

**Q3.** Compute the Haar subbands of the block $\begin{pmatrix} 4 & 4\\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
LL $= \tfrac12(a+b+c+d)$, V $= \tfrac12(a-b+c-d)$, H $= \tfrac12(a+b-c-d)$, D $= \tfrac12(a-b-c+d)$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
LL $= 4$, V $= 0$, H $= 4$, D $= 0$: a horizontal edge (bright top, dark bottom) lights only H.
:::

---

**Q4.** A $512 \times 512$ image is transformed with 5 levels. How big is the final LL, and how many coefficients are there in total?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Each level halves both sides of LL.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$512/2^5 = 16$: LL is $16 \times 16$. Total: still $512^2 = 262\,144$ coefficients, a change of basis.
:::

---

**Q5.** Why are the detail coefficients of a photograph or micrograph mostly small, with a few very large ones?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What does a detail coefficient see in a flat region, and at an edge?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Most of an image is smooth or flat locally, where the high-pass filters give near-zero output. Large details appear only where the filter covers an edge or a small structure, which is a small part of the image. The histogram is sharply peaked at 0 with heavy tails: the image is sparse in the wavelet basis.
:::

---

**Q6.** With 3 % of the coefficients, a Haar reconstruction looks blocky and a db4 reconstruction blurred. Why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What do the basis functions look like?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
A reconstruction is a sum of the kept basis functions. Haar basis functions are piecewise-constant squares, so missing details leave square steps; db4 basis functions are smooth bumps, so missing details leave a smooth blur (with slight ringing from their small side lobes).
:::

---

**Q7.** Keeping 5 % of the coefficients is not a compression ratio of 20. Why not?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What else must be stored?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The decoder also needs the **positions** of the kept coefficients (16 bits each for a $256 \times 256$ image), and the values need bits too. With 8 bits per value and 16 per position, 5 % gives a ratio of about 6.7. Real codecs quantise and entropy-code to do better (compression day).
:::

---

**Q8.** *(math)* Show that the 2D Haar subbands of a $2 \times 2$ block form an orthonormal change of basis, by writing the four "basis images".

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Each subband value is $\langle$block, basis image$\rangle$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The basis images are $\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & 1\end{pmatrix}$ (LL), $\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1 & -1\\1 & -1\end{pmatrix}$ (V), $\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1 & 1\\-1 & -1\end{pmatrix}$ (H), $\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 1\end{pmatrix}$ (D). Each has squared entries summing to $4 \cdot \tfrac14 = 1$, and any two have an entrywise product summing to 0 (two $+$ and two $-$ products). So they are orthonormal in $\mathbb R^4$, and the block is the sum of the subband values times its basis images.
:::
